day.text: I'm the Eagle. I visited Alex, and the only visitor was Ellis, which is why I got the +1. Ellis named Alex as the Mouser right before collapsing, which fits a Wink. I'm throwing at Alex.
day.note: Ellis collapsed right after naming Alex as the Mouser, which fits a Mouser's Wink, so I'm reading Alex as Meowfia. My Eagle visit confirmed Ellis was the one visitor to Alex, so I'll back the throw at Alex.
Casey is already throwing at me, and any extra talk from me risks exposure. I'll stay quiet on the last beat and decide my throw in the eggsecution.

Alex is the consensus target and likely Meowfia. My stake only banks if the eggsecuted player is Farm and my target is that player, so I'll risk only my Wild, which returns my highest card if I'm on the other team.
Nothing new to add; the table has already converged on Alex. Stay quiet.
I've already stated my throw at Alex, and repeating it adds nothing. I'll stay quiet on the last beat.

day.text: Casey, your Eagle +1 rests on Ellis visiting Alex, and Ellis is dead and can't confirm it. That makes Ellis's Mouser claim unverifiable from both sides. I'd like more from Casey before we throw at Alex.
day.note: Casey is pushing hard on Alex based on Ellis's dead claim, which can't be verified. I'll note that Casey's Eagle story rests on a dead player, and not add a caw.

Alex.note: I'm Meowfia Mouser with Drew as partner and know nothing about this round's roles yet. I'll visit Finley to learn their role.

Casey.note: I'm the Eagle, Farm, with no information. I'm visiting Alex to learn their visitors and gain eggs.

Drew.note: I'm the Sphinx with Alex as my Meowfia partner. Farm roles in play are Eagle, Kookaburra, Owl, Turkey. I'll pick Eagle to identify a Farm player.

Ellis.note: As Farm Kookaburra, I learn one player's role. Alex was Meowfia last round, so I'll check Alex.

Finley.note: Round 3 as Owl, Farm. No info yet, so visit Casey at random to learn which animals visited them.

audit: Casey lays 1 egg in Casey's nest

lines: No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.
Finley is the Owl.
You hold 1 Wink.
No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.
1 egg was laid in your nest: you drew S2 (2).
Alex was visited by: Ellis.
No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.
The Eagle is Casey.
No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.
Alex is the Mouser.
No eggs were laid in or taken from your nest.
Animals that visited Casey: Sphinx.

Alex.feeling: Tense and precarious: Farm has pinned Ellis's death on me, and I'm trying to keep my partner Drew from being exposed.

Blair.feeling: Messy and contradictory: the claims don't line up, and with Ellis dead the best evidence is gone, so I'm working from thin reads.

Casey.feeling: Messy and fast: Blair and Ellis have both gone quiet or dropped out, and the Alex-versus-Casey vote is hard to read.

Drew.feeling: Tense and a little awkward, since I know my Meowfia partner and have to argue the table's case against them without drawing attention.

Ellis.feeling: Messy and contradictory: Ellis's death removed my confirmed read, so the table is leaning on unverifiable claims.

Finley.feeling: Round 3 is murky: Ellis died after naming Alex, and the Eagle and Hawk claims can't be checked, so I'm playing on a thin read.

Alex.note: Meowfia wins the round when a Farm player is eggsecuted, and ties go to a Farm player. Casey is pushing me and is Farm, so I'll throw at Casey with three cards, which banks at 2x if Casey is eggsecuted and returns my highest card otherwise.

Blair.note: Under the rule shown now, a Farm stake banks at full value if the target is Meowfia, so I'll commit my two highest cards on Alex, who I think is Meowfia.

Casey.note: I'm fairly confident Alex is the Meowfia Mouser who winked Ellis, so I'll throw at Alex with a meaningful stake, H7b.

Drew.note: Casey is Farm, so throwing at Casey gives me a 2x bank if Casey is eggsecuted, and my highest card returns if not. I'll throw C7b and D4.

Ellis.note: I'm dead, so I have no vote, but my throw still scores. Alex is my best read for Meowfia, and a throw at the other team returns my highest card, so a single low card at Alex is nearly free.

Finley.note: Throw at Alex, the table's convergence and the Ellis death pattern point there. Small stake: D5.

Alex.confusing: The confused-report mechanic was hard to trust: I couldn't tell whether my own dawn info was wrong, so every visit claim was shaky. Tracking who-visited-whom across claims was also tangled.
Alex.fun: Ellis naming me as the Mouser right before collapsing from a Wink felt like a real Meowfia-style reveal. Watching the table split on Casey and Blair's visit stories was the most engaging part.
Alex.change: Make dawn reports say whether a visit was to you or from you, so players can check claims faster. Also make the Wink's target clearer, since I accidentally targeted my own name in round 2.
Alex.regret: In round 2 I winked "Alex," which was my own name, so that Wink was wasted and I never removed Ellis. I should have named Ellis carefully and avoided the self-target.

Blair.confusing: The stake rules changed between rounds: round 1 banked a Farm stake at 2x only when the target was the eggsecuted Farm player, but round 3 said it banks at full value whenever the target is Meowfia. I also briefly misread how the Eagle gains eggs, and had to correct myself at the table.
Blair.fun: Round 1 as the Sphinx: I learned Casey was the Hawk, then helped vote Casey out for a Meowfia win, and my doubled 19-point bank made it my best moment.
Blair.change: State the banking and Grudge rules once, clearly, and keep them the same every round so players can plan their throws.
Blair.regret: In round 2 I invented a House Cat claim that nobody could check, which drew four votes onto me and exposed my position. I would stay quieter and avoid a claim I could not back up.

Casey.confusing: The Eagle's egg rule was easy to get backwards, since Finley claimed an Eagle gains from its own visitors. The Sphinx and Kookaburra reports were also hard to check, because the game never shows what each player's visit revealed.
Casey.fun: Round 3, when Ellis named Alex as the Mouser and then collapsed, and the table had to work out whether that was a Wink. Alex's cats were exposed by the vote that followed.
Casey.change: Show each player's egg change and visitor list to everyone at dawn, so claims like the Eagle's and Owl's can be checked without guessing. Also make the Wink's use visible, so a collapse isn't just a guess.
Casey.regret: In Round 1 I muddled my Hawk story by mixing "hugged" with "visited Drew," which invited suspicion I didn't need. I would state my visit and result once, cleanly, and stop changing the wording.

Drew.confusing: The 2x banking rule for Meowfia throws and how the consolation card return works were hard to track. I also wasn't sure whether a dead player's Eagle or Mouser claims could still be checked.
Drew.fun: Round 3 as the Sphinx: I learned Casey was the Eagle and watched the table chase a Mouser claim that died with its maker. Keeping my partner Alex alive while steering suspicion elsewhere was tense.
Drew.change: I'd make the Owl and similar information roles report more clearly what they learned about visitors, since my dawn reports were narrow and caused a lot of confusion.
Drew.regret: In round 1 I threw two cards at Casey, who was Farm, so the stake was simply discarded. As a Farm player I should have thrown at a suspect I believed was Meowfia, like Blair, to bank the stake.

Ellis.confusing: The Eagle and Owl egg rules were the hardest to track, especially whether an Eagle's egg comes from visitors to its target or to itself. Casey's Eagle claim and Finley's Owl read caused a day-3 argument about it.
Ellis.fun: Round 2, where the table converged on Blair's unverifiable House Cat claim and eggsecuted Blair as Meowfia, was a satisfying read. Farm then won the round.
Ellis.change: I'd make the dawn reports name the visitor's role or action more explicitly, so players aren't left guessing whether an egg came from a visit or a Hawk-style effect. A clearer dead-player vote rule would also help.
Ellis.regret: In Round 3 I publicly named Alex as the Mouser on day 1, which made me an obvious target and got me Winked before I could vote. I'd keep the Kookaburra read quieter and throw at Alex with a low card instead.

Finley.confusing: Dawn egg changes were hard to cross-check, since Eagle and Owl gains depend on who visited whom, and the claims often conflicted. I also couldn't tell whether a Sphinx's visit to Casey would have counted for anyone else.
Finley.fun: Round 2 went well: Drew, Alex, and Casey's Owl, Turkey, and Falcon claims fit together, and our vote on Blair caught a Meowfia player. Watching the claims line up was satisfying.
Finley.change: I would make dawn reports list who visited a player when the role depends on it, so visit claims are easier to check. Ellis's collapse also had no visible cause, which I'd like explained at the table.
Finley.regret: In round 1 I joined the pile-on against Casey, a Farm player, instead of pressing Ellis, who was vague and was Meowfia. I would press Ellis on the role and visit question before voting.

review.title: The Blair Runaway
review.headline: Blair banked 38 points in round one and nobody ever caught up.
review.summary: Round 1 was a muddle of hug and visit claims. The table piled onto Farm Hawk Casey, and Meowfia won. Blair's two high cards banked at 2x for 38 points, and that lead decided the game. Farm won rounds 2 and 3 by eggsecuting the cat with the weakest story, but nobody could close the gap. Blair finished 50 points ahead.

rounds.recap: Casey (Hawk) was hugged and Alex (Kookaburra) was confused, so reports contradicted each other. Casey's honest but shifting story drew suspicion. Both cats, Blair and Ellis, joined the pile on Casey. Casey was eggsecuted and Meowfia won. Blair's 9 and 10 banked at 2x for 38 points.

The Owl, Falcon and Eagle claims cross-checked. Alex's fake Turkey claim fit his +1 egg. Blair was last to claim and said House Cat, which sounded like a cat on his own words. Four players threw at him and Farm won. Alex's wink seems to have done nothing.

Ellis, Kookaburra, named Alex as the Mouser. Alex winked Ellis right after, which made it look true. Casey's Eagle +1 fit Ellis's visit. Farm converged on Alex and eggsecuted him. Drew, his partner, defended him only weakly.

highlights.text: Blair, the Sphinx, threw 9 and 10 at the Farm player everyone suspected and banked 38 points, deciding the game.
Blair claimed House Cat as the only unclaimed role, so he outed himself as a cat and the table voted him out.
Alex winked Ellis right after Ellis named him Mouser, and the timing exposed him.
Finley's Owl read of a Sphinx visit was true but was mistaken for a lie over a misread Eagle rule.

confusions.what: Said an Eagle gains only from visitors to itself. The Eagle gains from visitors to its target.
Agreed with Finley's wrong Eagle reading in beat 1, then argued against it later.
Repeated Finley's wrong Eagle rule at first and had to correct it.
Named himself as the wink target instead of Ellis, so the Wink was wasted or unclear.
Opened with 'Blair's gone', which is an odd self-reference that doesn't fit the game.
Said a hug on a Hawk who visited Drew implied Drew was the Floofer. Hugs come from visitors to the Hawk.
Thought a Farm stake banks only if the target is Meowfia, and ignored how cats score.

worked: The Wink created the best moment of round 3: a kill right after an accusation was a strong clue.
Cross-checking visits and egg counts (Owl, Falcon, Eagle in round 2) gave Farm real evidence.
The 2x bank for Meowfia stakes makes a winning cat's high throw a big, risky bet.
The Floofer hug in round 1 created a real contradiction puzzle.
problems: Round 1's 38-point swing from one 2x bank decided the whole game. Cap the bank, or lower the multiplier, so later rounds can matter.
The leader was never targeted. Blair at 46 points was hard to spot because scores are only announced at the start of rounds, and nobody acted on it. Consider more visible standings.
Cats claiming the last unclaimed role is an easy tell. Blair's House Cat claim sank him. Showing the Meowfia a safe farm animal helps but is not enough when all the farm roles are claimed.
Eagle and Owl rules were misread, so egg-count checks felt shaky. Clearer wording of 'visitors to their target' would help.
Dead players still throw and score, and a Wink kill is easy to read. The Mouser's Wink is too weak when it reveals itself by timing, so a delay or hidden timing would help.
